hints.title: Filtering Orders to Year 2020
hints.text: Identify all sellers who have at least one sale with sale_date between 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31.

hints.title: Anti-Join Exclusion
hints.text: Select sellers from Seller whose seller_id is not in the set of active 2020 sellers.

hints.title: Alphabetical Sorting
hints.text: Order the resulting seller names in ascending alphabetical order.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT seller_name
FROM Seller
WHERE seller_id NOT IN (
    SELECT seller_id
    FROM Orders
    WHERE sale_date >= '2020-01-01' AND sale_date <= '2020-12-31'
)
ORDER BY seller_name ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Hash anti-join excludes sellers active in 2020 and sorts non-active sellers alphabetically.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Joining all orders without date filtering excludes sellers who had sales in other years but none in 2020.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Subquery filtering isolates 2020 transactions into a hash set for linear exclusion.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Not in or left join anti-join with calendar interval boundaries.

import pandas as pd

def sellers_with_no_sales(customer: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame, seller: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    orders['sale_date'] = orders['sale_date'].astype(str)
    orders_2020 = orders[orders['sale_date'].str.startswith('2020')]
    active_sellers = set(orders_2020['seller_id'])
    inactive = seller[~seller['seller_id'].isin(active_sellers)]
    return inactive[['seller_name']].sort_values(by='seller_name')
